# Best Open-Ear Earbuds for Running (October 2026)

| Pick | Why | Price seen | Battery | Water rating |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Bose Ultra Open Earbuds** | Best sound, stable clip fit | ~$199 (from $299) | 7 to 7.5 hrs | IPX4 |
| **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2** | Most awareness (bone conduction) | ~$125 to $180 | 12 hrs | IP55 |
| **Shokz OpenDots 2** | Long runs and rain | ~$200 | 10 hrs (40 with case) | IP57 |
| **Nothing Ear (Open)** | Strong bass and EQ for the price | ~$99 | Long | IP54 |
| **Soundcore AeroFit 2** | Budget ear-hook pick | ~$80 | 10 hrs (42 with case) | IP55 |

**Bose Ultra Open Earbuds: best overall.** Runner's World's top pick, with 2,221 logged miles. They don't bounce, they work with hats and glasses, and they leak less sound than most open designs. They have physical buttons, which are easier to use mid-stride. The downsides are a weak water rating, modest battery and limited volume in loud traffic. Runner's World also notes Bose plans a new open-ear model soon, so a short wait might be worth it.
- Reviews: [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- Where to buy: $199 at Bose, Best Buy and Amazon, per those pages.

**Shokz OpenRun Pro 2: best for traffic awareness.** These leave your ears completely open, have physical controls and use USB-C. Bass is fuller than older bone-conduction models, but clarity is a bit behind the Bose. The band can clash with ponytails, hoods and high collars.
- Reviews: [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/), [RTINGS vs. Bose](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946)
- Where to buy: about $125 at Walmart, REI and Best Buy, versus $180 at Amazon.

**Shokz OpenDots 2: best for marathon training or wet weather.** WIRED's overall pick. They have the best water resistance in these roundups and survived full submersion. Either bud fits either ear.
- Review: [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- Where to buy: $200 at Amazon, Best Buy and Shokz.

**Nothing Ear (Open): best value.** SoundGuys rates them the best workout earbuds for running. They have unusually good bass for open-ear buds, a full parametric EQ and multipoint pairing.
- Reviews: [SoundGuys workout earbuds](https://www.soundguys.com/best-workout-earbuds-2719/), [SoundGuys open-ear picks](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)
- Where to buy: $99 at Amazon (MSRP $149).

**Soundcore AeroFit 2: budget pick.** The ear hooks are secure, and you get IP55, LDAC and wireless charging.
- Review: [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)
- Where to buy: $79.99 at Amazon.
- A deal site, [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2), lists code AFSC20 for Soundcore's own store. That only brings the $129.99 store price down to about $104, so Amazon is cheaper. The Dealectric link is also an affiliate link.

**Even cheaper:** If you just want to see whether you like open-ear buds, the JLab Flex Open is about $40 at Amazon and Walmart, per [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/).

**My quick take:**
- Road running in traffic: OpenRun Pro 2.
- Best sound and comfort: Bose Ultra Open.
- Rainy climate or long efforts: OpenDots 2.
- Best value: Nothing Ear (Open).

I could only see the review pages, not direct product pages, so use the retailer buttons on those reviews and check the current price at checkout.
